article.headline: Eli Lilly Jumps 6.6% After Selling 53% More At Lower Prices
article.deck: Lilly closed 6.3% past the 1,292.75 buy point of a nine-week flat base, beyond the 1,357.39 top of the buy range; the entry is gone until a pullback or a new base.
body: Eli Lilly rose 85.40, or 6.6%, to 1,373.70 Thursday after its third-quarter report, on volume 1.84 times the 50-day average. The drugmaker is worth $1.22 trillion, and its relative strength line hit a new high on the day.

Lilly discovers, develops, makes and sells prescription drugs in the U.S., Europe, China, Japan and elsewhere. The center of the business is cardiometabolic medicine: Mounjaro and Trulicity for type 2 diabetes, Zepbound for obesity, Jardiance, and a long line of insulins under the Humalog and Humulin names. It also sells cancer drugs, including Cyramza.

The growth is in the sales line. June-quarter revenue rose 47.7% from a year earlier to $22.974 billion, and EPS rose 26.2% to 7.94 a share. Revenue climbed in every quarter in the table, from $17.6008 billion in September 2025 to $19.292 billion, $19.799 billion and $22.974 billion. EPS ran 6.21, 7.39 and 8.26 before easing to 7.94 in June. The third-quarter figures reported Thursday are not in the table.

The headlines point the same way. One summed up the quarter as Lilly selling 53% more at lower prices. Its CFO said cancer drugs are the next growth drivers and, on the company's acquisitions, said Lilly is taking bets on future revenue. Another headline asked how much GLP-1 drugs can raise the bar for health care stocks.
The market pays up for that growth: 46.1 times trailing earnings and 28.9 times forward. Shares are up 27.8% this year and 67.5% over 12 months, and the stock ranks 89 of 99 on the desk's list.

On the chart, Lilly cleared a nine-week flat base at 1,292.75 on Oct. 22, on volume 1.13 times average. The base ran 13.9% deep, from an Aug. 19 high to a Sept. 11 low. Five sessions later the stock sits 6.3% past the buy point and above the 1,357.39 top of the buy range, 2.5% under its 52-week high of 1,408.38. It trades 15.1% above its 50-day line and 10.1% above its 21-day, and it ended 1.93 ATRs from the 21-day line, a strong trend but not a stretched one. After hours it added 0.3% to 1,377.34.
Lilly is extended. The base's entry is gone until the stock pulls back toward the buy range or forms a new base.
article.watch: A pullback into the 1,292.75 to 1,357.39 range or a test of the 21-day line at 1,248.09.

article.headline: Amgen Climbs 2% After Hours As Third-Quarter Report Nears
article.deck: Amgen traded at 471.10 after hours, just over the 469.49 top of the buy range from the 447.13 buy point of an eight-week cup, after closing inside the range at 460.73.
body: Amgen rose 10.37, or 2.3%, to 471.10 in after-hours trading as of 4:55 p.m. ET, on top of a regular-session gain of 8.90, or 2.0%, to 460.73. The after-hours price sits above the 468.27 52-week high and just past the 469.49 top of the buy range. The stock cleared an eight-week cup with a 447.13 buy point on Oct. 22; the base ran 16.2% deep from its Aug. 25 high to its Sept. 16 low. Thursday's volume was 1.06 times the 50-day average, and the breakout session traded 1.11 times.

At the close Amgen stood 3.0% past the buy point, five sessions after the breakout and 1.6% below the 52-week high. It trades 9.9% above its 50-day line and 23.2% above its 200-day, and the session left it 2.21 ATRs from the 21-day line: a strong trend, not yet a stretched one. The relative strength line set a new high, and the stock ranks 88 of 99 on the desk's list. Shares are up 40.8% this year and 57.7% over 12 months.

In the June quarter Amgen earned 4.37 a share, up 64.9% from a year earlier, on revenue of $10.054 billion, up 9.5%. The table's earlier quarters show EPS of 3.34 in March, 2.45 in December and 5.93 in September 2025. The third-quarter report is due Nov. 3.

The news is all ahead of that report: Amgen announced the webcast for its 2026 third-quarter results and declared its fourth-quarter dividend, and one preview headline asked whether rising expenses point to a profit squeeze.
A close back under 447.13 would undo the breakout.
article.watch: Whether Friday's regular session holds above the 469.49 top of the buy range, then the Nov. 3 report.

article.deck: United Rentals cleared the 1,179.28 buy point of a 12-week cup Thursday and closed 1.6% past it, inside a buy range that runs to 1,238.24.
body: United Rentals rose 24.07, or 2.0%, to 1,198.68, ten cents under its 1,198.78 52-week high. The move took it through the 1,179.28 buy point of a 12-week cup that ran 58 sessions and corrected 17.9% from its Aug. 7 high to its Sept. 3 low. Volume was light, at 0.83 times the 50-day average.

This is day one of the breakout, and the close sits 1.6% past the buy point, well inside the range that tops out at 1,238.24. The stock trades 14.4% above its 50-day line and 23.6% above its 200-day, and it ended 2.07 ATRs from the 21-day line, an intact trend short of stretched. The relative strength line hit a new high, and the stock ranks 86 of 99 on the desk's list. Shares are up 48.1% this year, 19.8% in the past month and 36.9% over 12 months.

The September quarter brought EPS of 14.77, up 35.4% from a year earlier, on revenue of $4.893 billion, up 15.7%. Earnings rose through 2026: 8.43 a share in March, 12.03 in June and 14.77 in September. Revenue climbed from $3.985 billion to $4.41 billion to $4.893 billion over the same three quarters.
On Monday the company priced an offering of $700 million of 5.550% senior notes due 2029, $800 million of 5.750% notes due 2031 and $1 billion of 6.200% notes due 2036.
A close back below 1,179.28 would turn the breakout into a stall.

article.headline: Cheniere Jumps 7% To New High After Raising Guidance And Dividend
article.deck: Cheniere cleared the 300.99 buy point of a 30-week cup and closed 6.0% past it, above the 316.04 top of the buy range on breakout day; the entry is gone until a pullback or a new base.
body: Cheniere Energy rose 21.17, or 7.1%, to 318.94, clearing the 300.99 buy point of a 30-week cup in a single session. The base ran 148 sessions and 25.7% deep, from a March 30 high to a June 18 low. Volume was 2.47 times the 50-day average. The close came 0.7% under the 321.22 52-week high and above the 316.04 top of the buy range, so the stock broke out and went extended on the same day.

Measured against its own daily range, the move is not stretched: the session ended 1.92 ATRs from the 21-day line, though the price sits 10.3% above that line and 13.5% above the 50-day. The stock ranks 89 of 99 on the desk's list, but the relative strength line is 11.4% below its high and has lagged the price. Shares are up 64.1% this year and 47.7% over 12 months. After hours it was flat at 319.05.

The latest quarter in the table, June, shows EPS of 14.65, up 100.7% from a year earlier, on revenue of $5.732 billion, up 23.5%. The March quarter was a loss of 16.65 a share; December earned 10.68 and September 2025 earned 4.75. Revenue rose from $4.441 billion to $5.732 billion across the four quarters. The third-quarter figures are not in the table.

Cheniere reported third-quarter results before the open, raised its full-year 2026 financial guidance and raised its quarterly dividend by over 12%, according to the company's release. A separate headline said it missed third-quarter earnings estimates.
A pullback into the 300.99 to 316.04 range would put the stock back where the base offered it.

article.headline: ServiceNow Plunges 26.9% As Third-Quarter Earnings Fall 43.7%
article.deck: The drop cut through the 50-day and 200-day lines and left the stock 26.7% below the 149.70 buy point of a seven-week cup it cleared Oct. 21; the breakout has failed and there is no buy point in play.
body: ServiceNow fell 40.46, or 26.9%, to 109.67 after its third-quarter report, on volume 5.5 times the 50-day average. The stock had cleared a seven-week cup at 149.70 on Oct. 21; that base ran 15.3% deep from its Aug. 31 high to its Sept. 28 low and formed well below the 210.20 high of July 24, 2025, after a slide to 81.24 on April 10. The close sits 26.7% under the buy point, six sessions after the breakout. After hours it lost another 1.59, or 1.5%, to 108.08.

The stock now trades 21.2% below its 50-day line at 139.18 and 4.7% below its 200-day at 115.13. It is 23.5% under its 21-day line, with the session's high 2.55 ATRs below it. The close is 43.2% off the 52-week high of 192.97. The stock ranks 24 of 99 on the desk's list, and the relative strength line is 48.2% below its high. Shares are down 28.4% this year and 41.5% over 12 months.

September-quarter EPS fell 43.7% to 0.27 a share, while revenue rose 20.5% to $4.106 billion. Revenue rose in each of the four quarters in the table, from $3.568 billion to $4.106 billion, while EPS went from 0.38 to 0.45, 0.29 and 0.27. The next report is listed for Jan. 27.

One headline said ServiceNow can't escape the SaaSpocalypse even after strong third-quarter AI growth, and Truist said its AI momentum is still too small to inflect overall growth. Another listed Google, ServiceNow and Fortinet among the earnings reports that hit the Nasdaq.
article.watch: Whether the stock can get back above the 200-day line at 115.13; until it does, the chart has no setup.

article.deck: Apple closed 1.0% past the 345.44 buy point of a four-week flat base, inside a buy range that runs to 362.71, with earnings due Nov. 2.
body: Apple rose 5.08, or 1.5%, to 348.91, 0.8% below its 52-week high of 351.73. The stock cleared a four-week flat base at 345.44 on Oct. 22; the base ran 22 sessions and only 5.7% deep, from a Sept. 22 high to an Oct. 1 low. Volume was 1.03 times the 50-day average Thursday and 1.17 times on breakout day.

Five sessions after the breakout, the close sits 1.0% past the buy point and well inside the range. Apple trades 5.0% above its 50-day line and 2.1% above its 21-day, and it ended 0.89 ATRs from the 21-day line, a calm trend nowhere near stretched. The stock ranks 74 of 99 on the desk's list, and the relative strength line is 2.2% below its high. Shares are up 28.3% this year and 29.7% over 12 months, for a market value of $5.09 trillion. The table's earlier quarters show EPS of 2.01 in March, 2.84 in the December holiday quarter on $143.756 billion in sales, and 1.85 in September 2025. The next report is due Nov. 2.

Apple unveiled its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, priced at $2,899, and one headline said the iPhone Duo is likely to deliver growth acceleration on strong demand. Another said Nvidia is getting close to being surpassed by Apple in market value.
With earnings two sessions out, the base is tight and the breakout is intact.

article.headline: Spotify Climbs 3.5% A Week After Third-Quarter Earnings Miss
article.deck: Spotify bounced off its 50-day line but sits 3.3% below the 576.10 buy point of a seven-week cup it cleared Oct. 22; the breakout stays stalled until the stock closes back above that level.
body: Spotify rose 18.84, or 3.5%, to 557.24 on volume 0.72 times the 50-day average. The stock cleared a seven-week cup at 576.10 on Oct. 22, on volume 3.1 times average; the base ran 18.4% deep from its Sept. 3 high to its Oct. 5 low. It formed well below the 748.30 high of Aug. 15, 2025, after a slide to 405.00 on Feb. 5. Five sessions after the breakout, the close is 3.3% under the buy point.

Thursday's gain came off the 50-day line at 529.38; the stock now sits 5.3% above it and 12.1% above the 200-day. It ended just 0.02 ATRs above the 21-day line, essentially resting on it. The close is 17.2% below the 52-week high of 673.16. Spotify ranks 54 of 99 on the desk's list, and the relative strength line is 25.3% below its high. Shares are down 4.0% this year and 14.7% over 12 months.

September-quarter EPS fell 24.4% to 2.48 euros a share, while revenue rose 16.3% to 4.969 billion euros. EPS has declined in each quarter in the table, from 4.43 to 3.45, 2.61 and 2.48, while revenue rose from 4.531 billion to 4.969 billion euros.
Headlines said the stock rose 11% after the Oct. 22 report, erasing its 2026 loss in a day, and that it rose 6% despite an earnings miss.
article.watch: A close back above 576.10 restarts the breakout; a close under the 50-day line at 529.38 ends it.

stories.angle: still in buy range after breakout

article.headline: Exxon Holds Near High Ahead Of Friday's Third-Quarter Report
article.deck: Exxon sits 3.8% past the 176.51 buy point of a 27-week cup, inside a buy range that tops out at 185.34, with earnings due Oct. 30.
body: Exxon Mobil rose 1.27, or 0.7%, to 183.29 on volume 0.83 times the 50-day average, 0.9% below its 52-week high of 184.88. The stock cleared a 27-week cup at 176.51 on Oct. 14, on volume in line with its average; the base ran 137 sessions and 23.5% deep, from a March 30 high to a June 25 low. After hours it added 1.22, or 0.7%, to 184.51.

Eleven sessions after the breakout, the close is 3.8% past the buy point and still in range. Exxon trades 9.5% above its 50-day line and 4.4% above its 21-day, and it ended 1.37 ATRs from the 21-day line, an orderly trend. It ranks 86 of 99 on the desk's list, though the relative strength line is 12.2% below its high. Shares are up 52.3% this year and 59.3% over 12 months.

In the June quarter Exxon earned 3.48 a share, up 112.2% from a year earlier, on revenue of $114.529 billion, up 44.1%. The table's earlier quarters show EPS of 1.00 in March, 1.53 in December and 1.76 in September 2025. Third-quarter results are due Friday.
Exxon and Chevron canceled trips to a UAE oil show over safety concerns, according to a report, and William Blair launched coverage of U.S. oil majors, saying it sees value in cost leaders.
article.watch: Friday's report: a close above 185.34 takes it out of the buy range, and a close under 176.51 stalls the breakout.

market_note: The Nasdaq fell 1.4% to 26,184.72 and closed 1.5% below its 50-day line, while the S&P 500 and the Dow each slipped 0.3%, to 7,720.39 and 52,342.56, holding 0.3% and 0.2% above their 50-day lines. The S&P 500 carries 5 distribution days over the last 25 sessions, the Nasdaq 3 and the Dow 4, with the Dow's latest logged Thursday. The desk's read stays at Uptrend under pressure. Leadership this week came from health care, energy and big-cap names rather than chips: Eli Lilly, Cheniere, Amgen, United Rentals, Apple and Tesla all cleared buy points, energy has 79% of its names above the 50-day line, and the AI chip group, with the highest average RS, has only 25% above it after Marvell broke down. After hours, Reddit fell 17.4%, Stryker 12.3%, Arm 6.9%, Dell 6.8%, AMD 5.5% and Amazon 5.2%.

chief.verdict: Leadership is narrowing and rotating away from tech. The breakouts that work are in industrials, energy and drugs (URI, LNG, AMGN, LLY, XOM). Software and AI chips are breaking down: ServiceNow fell 26.9%, Fortinet 20.1% and Marvell 13.2% through its 50-day line, and after hours Dell, AMD and Arm each fell another 5.5% to 6.9%. Most of the clean-looking setups report earnings within five sessions, so today's list holds few real entries, and the risk leans to the downside.
chief.market: With the desk at Uptrend under pressure, 5 distribution days on the S&P 500 and 3 on the Nasdaq, and the Nasdaq down 1.4% to 1.5% below its 50-day line, keep exposure light and limit new buys to one or two small starter positions.

picks.why: This is the best chart on the list. United Rentals broke out today from a 12-week cup 17.9% deep and closed at 1198.68, 1.6% past the buy point with its RS line at a new high and an RS rank of 86. Earnings are already out (latest quarter EPS up 35.4%, revenue up 15.7%), so there is no report inside the window, and at 2.07 ATRs from the 21-day line the move is not stretched. The risk is that the stock sits 14.4% above its 50-day in a market under pressure, so a reversal back under the pivot would come fast.
picks.entry: Buy range is 1179.28 to 1238.24, and the stock has to hold above 1179.28. A close back under 1179.28 ends the trade.

picks.why: GitLab has an RS rank of 96, closed at 56.65 inside a 5-week cup's buy range, 1.8% past the 55.65 buy point, and has no earnings in the coming week. The risk is the group: software was the sector that broke down today, so this one stays a small position.
picks.entry: Buy range is 55.65 to 58.43. A close back under 55.65 means the stock has failed.

picks.why: Analog Devices has an RS rank of 90 in an 18-week cup and closed at 433.28, 2.9% below the 446.01 buy point. It is on the desk's aggressive list, but the payload gives no early-entry level, so no position goes on before the pivot. The risk is that it is a chip stock on a night when AMD, Arm and Dell are all lower after hours.
picks.entry: Wait for a decisive close above 446.01 and buy no higher than the top of the range at 468.31.

picks.why: Cheniere jumped 7.1% to 318.94 on its earnings day. The move cleared a 30-week cup at 300.99 but closed past the 316.04 top of the buy range, so it is extended at the first breakout. The base is 25.7% deep and the RS line is still 11.4% below its high, so the chart is valid but loose, and the earnings risk is behind it.
picks.entry: Wait for a pullback toward 300.99 or the 21-day line at 289.11 that holds, and do not buy above 316.04.

avoid.why: Exxon reports Oct. 30, and the stock closed at 183.29, near the 185.34 top of its buy range, which leaves little room in front of the report.
Amgen reports Nov. 3, inside five sessions, and the after-hours price of 471.10 is already past the 469.49 top of the buy range, so the entry is gone before the report.

Tesla's flat base breakout sits inside a bigger correction: it closed 19.2% under the 498.83 high, the latest quarter's EPS fell 43.6% and revenue fell 0.2%, and the 403.30 close is near the 406.28 top of its range.
Marvell's RS rank of 97 is cover for a broken chart: it fell 13.2% through its 50-day line to 218.34, 33.8% below the pivot of a 50.6%-deep cup, and was off another 3.8% after hours.

chief.watch: Watch whether the Nasdaq can get back above its 50-day line, which it closed 1.5% below, after AMD's 5.5% and Dell's 6.8% after-hours losses hit the open.
